metaDescription: Five FIFINE streaming mixers and kits compared on XLR input, phantom power, game and chat control and bundled microphones for a first stream setup.
expertTake: The FIFINE Ampligame SC8 is the best FIFINE streaming mixer here because a 48V XLR port, a game and chat balance knob and optical and 3.5mm inputs make it the most flexible box in the family. The Ampligame SC3 is the value pick for a single microphone. A streamer who already owns a mixer should buy only the microphone from these kits.
introParagraphs: This maker targets the first time streamer: a small desktop box with a microphone input, a few knobs and a USB cable, priced so that a whole setup costs less than a single studio preamp. The range is narrow but the choices inside it matter.

The differences come down to which extra inputs a box offers, whether it can power a condenser microphone and whether the kit includes a microphone at all. Those three points decide which model suits a console player, a PC streamer or a first time podcaster.

products.name: FIFINE Ampligame SC8 gaming mixer with 7.1 surround and XLR

specList.label: Console audio
specList.value: Optical AUX for PS4 and TV

products.description:
The SC8 is the most complete box the brand sells for a streamer. Its XLR port supplies 48V phantom power, so a condenser microphone works, an optical AUX input connects a console or TV, and a 3.5mm AUX input takes commentary or music. A dedicated Game/Chat knob shifts the balance between the two without opening software.

The feature list is broad and the controls stay simple. A headphone preamp helps drive demanding headsets, 7.1 surround processing and RGB lighting cater to gamers, and the mute button sits on the front. Compared with the SC3 it adds optical input, the balance knob and surround, at a higher price tier, but it still carries a single microphone input.

In use it behaves like a small hub. Decide which source feeds the optical port, set the Game/Chat balance once and mark the knob position with tape. Keep the surround processing for your own headset, since viewers hear the stream mix, and use a dynamic microphone if your room is noisy. If a console feeds the optical port, remember that the box then carries two audio worlds at once, the console and your PC, so test that both reach the stream and that neither is doubled. Over time the Game/Chat knob becomes the control you touch most, and a small pen mark beside it helps you return to a good starting balance.
products.bestFor: Gamers who want phantom power, optical input and a game and chat knob.
pros: Optical AUX for a console or TV
cons: Surround helps you more than your audience

products.name: FIFINE Ampligame SC3 XLR gaming mixer with Indi-Fader

specList.label: Controls
specList.value: Mute, volume and real time monitoring

specList.label: Connection
specList.value: USB plug and play for PC

products.description:
The SC3 gives a streamer four individually controllable channels, an XLR microphone input with built in 48V phantom power and the basics of mute, volume and real time monitoring. USB plug and play keeps setup to a single cable on a PC.

It does less than the SC8: there is no optical input and no dedicated balance knob, and the control surface is plain. In return it costs less and is quicker to understand, which suits a streamer who just wants a better microphone chain. The SC3W is the same machine in white.

It is a dependable first box. Use a balanced XLR cable, keep the slider near a marked position and use the front mute button during coughs or interruptions.
products.bestFor: First time streamers who want an XLR microphone path at a low price.
pros: Mute, volume and monitoring built in
cons: No optical input or balance knob

products.name: FIFINE USB audio interface and mixer for XLR microphone
products.description:
This FIFINE interface and mixer serves a dynamic or condenser XLR microphone with clean gain and phantom power. It works with PC and Mac, installs without a complicated setup and offers direct monitoring so you hear yourself without delay.

It is closer to a pure interface than a gaming mixer, so it lacks the RGB lighting, surround and sound effects of the SC8. That makes it a better fit for a podcaster than for a streamer who wants spectacle. Next to the SC3 it targets recording rather than games.

Pair it with a quality microphone and a boom arm. Set gain so peaks stay clear of the red and keep the USB cable short. Because direct monitoring plays your voice before it reaches the computer, mute the software monitor to avoid hearing a doubled, delayed echo. For recording, save a template in your editor with the input already selected, which turns each session into a single click.
products.bestFor: Mac and PC users who want a straightforward XLR interface for recording.
cons: Less feature rich than the SC8

products.name: FIFINE gaming audio mixer bundle with computer streaming microphone
products.description:
This bundle pairs a four channel RGB mixer with a computer streaming microphone for a one purchase start. The mixer has an XLR microphone interface with 48V phantom power and a smooth volume slider, and the microphone lists a frequency response of 50 Hz to 16 kHz.

The kit is built for one microphone. Its included condenser microphone is entry level, with a modest frequency range that covers speech and not much more, and condensers pick up more room noise than dynamics. Beside the SC3 alone it costs more but removes the need to choose a microphone.

Use it in a quiet room and add a pop filter and a stand. When the show grows, the mixer remains useful with a better microphone. A reasonable upgrade path is to keep the mixer and swap in a dynamic microphone, which improves a noisy room at once. Record a minute of silence with the kit microphone to learn its noise floor, and consider moving it off the desk surface onto a stand to avoid thumps and reflections.
products.bestFor: First time streamers who want mixer and microphone in one box.
pros: Mixer and microphone in one purchase
RGB mixer with a smooth slider
cons: Entry level condenser picks up room noise

products.name: FIFINE audio equipment bundle with RGB mixer and XLR dynamic mic
products.description:
This bundle pairs an RGB gaming mixer with an XLR dynamic vocal microphone that handles 120 dB of sound pressure. The high SPL rating makes it suited to loud or shouting voices, which is common in gaming.

A dynamic microphone rejects room noise better than a budget condenser, so it often sounds cleaner in an untreated gaming room. The tradeoff is that dynamics need more gain and sit close to the mouth. Compared with the condenser bundle it favors loud, noisy rooms over quiet, treated ones.

Keep the microphone a fist from your mouth and use a boom arm. Set the gain so a shout does not clip, and test with your loudest moment. A dynamic capsule has a narrow pickup, so small changes in distance change the level a lot, and a few days of practice builds a habit of speaking at a steady distance. The RGB lighting can be turned down or off if reflections bother your camera.
products.bestFor: Loud, noisy gaming rooms that suit a dynamic microphone.
cons: Dynamic needs close placement and gain

buyingCriteria.explanation: The SC8, SC3 and the interface list 48V phantom, so a condenser microphone works. If you plan to use a dynamic microphone only, phantom is not needed, though a switchable supply keeps the door open for a later change of microphone and costs nothing extra to have. Confirm the supply before pairing a condenser with a kit.
The SC8's optical AUX connects a console or TV, and its 3.5mm AUX takes commentary or music. The SC3 is mostly a microphone box. If you stream a console, choose the SC8 for its extra inputs.

A dedicated Game/Chat knob on the SC8 shifts emphasis between game sound and party voices without software. Boxes without it leave the balance to the operating system. A streamer who plays team games benefits most, because voice callouts matter as much as explosions and the right balance changes from one match to the next. A hardware knob makes that change instant.

The kit with a condenser suits a quiet room, while the kit with a dynamic rated to 120 dB SPL suits a loud one. A dynamic capsule rejects room noise but needs more gain. Match the microphone to your room, because the same kit can sound crisp in a closet and harsh in a bare room. If you are unsure, record a short sample in your actual space before deciding which microphone to keep using.

The FIFINE USB interface offers direct monitoring and PC and Mac support, while the Ampligame boxes add RGB, surround and game controls. A podcaster fits the interface, a gamer the SC8. The interface leaves out the lighting and surround features, which keeps the price and the desk clutter down, and its direct monitoring gives a clean path for recording voice and instruments.

Every unit in this family carries one microphone input. A co host needs a second box or a different brand. Plan your show before choosing, and think about who sits at the desk in six months, because a mixer chosen for a solo host becomes a bottleneck the moment a friend wants to join. If you often host guests, the practical route is two boxes on two USB ports with the stream software merging both microphones, though that is more setup than a single board with two inputs, so check whether another brand fits better.

howWeEvaluated.title: Input flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared XLR, optical and 3.5mm inputs, noting the SC8 as the most flexible. A streamer's desk often grows to include a console, a phone and a music source, and a box that already has the right connectors saves a second purchase later.

howWeEvaluated.title: Microphone support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked phantom power and the type of bundled microphone. The microphone is the biggest influence on how a stream sounds, so we asked whether the included one matches a typical room and whether the box leaves room to replace it later.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the Game/Chat knob, sliders and mute buttons. Small controls that can be used by feel during a match score higher than a long menu, and we noted that a front mounted mute button is easier to reach than one on the back.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered PC, Mac and console use. The Ampligame boxes are described for PC, the interface for PC and Mac and the SC8 adds an optical route, so we matched each unit to the platform it is clearly built for rather than assuming broad compatibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared price tiers, with the SC3 lowest and the SC8 and bundles higher. Because every unit is aimed at beginners, value meant getting a clean microphone path and sensible controls without paying for extras the buyer will not use, and the bundles were judged against buying the same parts separately.

cards.label: Mixer only
cards.text: The SC8 and SC3 let you choose your own microphone, which gives a better upgrade path.

cards.label: Kit
cards.text: The bundles include a microphone, which saves research but fixes your starting microphone.

howToChoose.note: Choose a mixer alone if you own a microphone and a kit if you are starting from nothing.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An optical or auxiliary input and a balance control for game and chat.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SC8 lists optical AUX and a Game/Chat knob, which no other FIFINE here does. A console player who wants one box for microphone, game sound and chat will find the SC8 the only clear fit, while the SC3 leaves console audio to a separate path.

cards.text: You use a console or want a balance knob. The SC8 pays for itself.

maintenance.why: Dust and crumbs affect sliders and knobs on a busy desk. Use compressed air and a soft brush, and keep a cover over the unit when the stream ends.
Worn cables drop out in the middle of a stream and cause crackle. Replace any that fail and keep a spare so a bad cable never ends a broadcast.
Wrong settings leave a condenser silent. Confirm the 48V switch matches the microphone and test with a short recording before going live.
Knobs drift when bumped, and a small change is easy to miss. Speak a test sentence at your normal volume and check the meter before each stream.
Dust dulls the lighting and collects around the controls. Wipe the surface with a dry microfiber cloth and avoid liquid cleaners near the ports.

faq.q: Which FIFINE streaming mixer is best?
faq.a: The SC8 is the most flexible, with a 48V XLR port, optical and 3.5mm inputs and a Game/Chat knob. The SC3 is the best value for a single microphone, and the USB interface suits a Mac user or a podcaster. Pick by the sources you need to connect rather than by the longest feature list. List every device on your desk, from console to phone to second microphone, and tick off the inputs each box offers. The model with the most ticks and the fewest adapters is the right one, even if another has more lights.

faq.q: Do FIFINE mixers support condenser microphones?
faq.a: Models with 48V phantom power do. The SC8, the SC3 and the USB interface list it, so a condenser microphone can be powered directly from the box. Phantom is only needed for condensers, and many gaming rooms suit a dynamic microphone better because it picks up less keyboard and fan noise.

The SC8 has an optical AUX input, listed for PS4 and TV, and a 3.5mm AUX input for commentary or music. That makes it the only FIFINE here with a clear console route. Check what digital audio output your console offers before buying, since not every console provides an optical port. Newer consoles often rely on HDMI for sound, in which case an HDMI audio extractor or a capture device is needed to reach the box, and that adds cost and cabling that the product page may not mention.

Kits save research but include entry level microphones. A kit is a good way to start if you own nothing, and a mixer alone is better value if you already have a microphone. In either case the microphone is the first part worth upgrading when the stream grows.

The USB interface lists PC and Mac, and it installs without a complicated setup. The Ampligame boxes are described for PC, so Mac users should check compatibility in the manual before buying a gaming mixer and consider the interface instead.

faq.q: How many microphones can I connect?
faq.a: One per box, since every unit in this family carries a single XLR input. A show with a co host needs a second box on a second computer port or a different brand with two inputs, so decide on the number of voices before you choose.
